subject: Incident chronicle, corrective commitments, and verification request - AcmeCloud
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Michael Torres <michael.torres@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Incident chronicle, corrective commitments, and verification request - AcmeCloud

Hi Michael,

Thank you again for your patience while we investigated the service disruption on 2026-11-10 that affected inference request throughput for your production workspace. Attached is a concise, customer-facing chronicle and a list of corrective commitments we will deliver over the next 90 days.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- What happened: a coordination bug in autoscaler leader election caused a transient split-brain among GPU pool controllers which led to uneven shard assignment and token throttling for a subset of long-lived sessions.
- Impact window: ~2026-11-10T03:24Z to 2026-11-10T04:08Z (partial degradation for 8% of requests).
- Customer-visible effect: increased tail latency and intermittent 503s for streaming responses during the window.

What we’ve attached: Incident_Chronicle_AcmeCloud_20261114.pdf — a 2-page narrative with a minute-by-minute timeline and supporting logs; Mitigation-Checklist-AcmeCloud.xlsx — action owners and target dates.

Key corrective commitments (short form):
1) Fix autoscaler leader election edge-case; smoke tests + canary by 2026-11-20.
2) Add cross-pool reconciliation to prevent split-state for long-lived sessions; targeted release 2026-12-04.
3) Improve alerting: new latency anomaly detector and per-tenant token-rate guardrails; staged rollout by 2026-11-30.
4) Offer you a verification run and replay of a sample workload in a controlled window with our engineers present; proposed dates below.

Would you and your SREs be available for a 60-minute verification session next week (options: Tue 2026-11-17 10:00–11:00 PST or Thu 2026-11-19 13:00–14:00 PST)? We will: present the fixes, run a controlled load against a clone of your config, and capture traces for you to validate.

If anything in the attached chronicle needs clarification, please flag it and I’ll update immediately — our goal is a single shared truth you can use for your audit/comms.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments: Incident_Chronicle_AcmeCloud_20261114.pdf (summary), Mitigation-Checklist-AcmeCloud.xlsx (spreadsheet)

> Thank you again for your patience while we investigated the service disruption on 2026-11-10 that affected inference request throughput for your production workspace. Attached is a concise, customer-facing chronicle and a list of corrective commitments we will deliver over the next 90 days.

Thanks Naomi — great write-up. One small correction for the timeline: our internal leader-election rollback began at 03:28Z, not 03:30Z; that shifts the remediation marker earlier by ~2 minutes. Also adding one follow-up item to the checklist: we should add a post-deployment verification script that asserts per-shard KV continuity for long-lived sessions (owner: SRE; target: 2026-11-22).

I’ve updated the draft spreadsheet in the shared drive link (internal only). If you want, I can push a revised PDF into the attachments before we send a final version to Acme.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Incident Response
Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Michael Torres <michael.torres@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, support@acmecloud.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Updated chronicle and confirmation of verification session - AcmeCloud

Michael — following up with the finalized chronicle and an updated action ledger after Ben’s note. I’ve attached the revised PDF which includes the corrected 03:28Z rollback marker and a short appendix that maps each action to an owner and acceptance criteria. See the key points below and the verification session proposal at the end.

Concise timeline (UTC):
- 2026-11-10T03:24:12Z — first elevated latency alert for a subset of long-lived sessions.
- 2026-11-10T03:26:03Z — autoscaler leader election started following network jitter during a control-plane upgrade.
- 2026-11-10T03:28:14Z — automatic rollback triggered; partial reconciliation began.
- 2026-11-10T04:08:01Z — traffic returned to normal.

Root cause narrative (one paragraph):
A latent timing assumption in the autoscaler leader election algorithm assumed bounded retry backoff. During the control-plane upgrade, transient network jitter extended leader election delays beyond that bound, causing two controllers to believe they were primary for overlapping shards. That split-view produced conflicting shard assignments and intermittent token routing failures for long-lived sessions.

Acceptance criteria for us to consider this closed for AcmeCloud:
- Completed code fix merged to canary branch, canary run without regressions for 72 hours.
- Independent verification run with your team where we reproduce a sampling workload and your SREs confirm continuity of streams and absence of token gaps.
- Instrumented alerts firing and annotated runbook updated for this failure mode.

Action ledger (high level):
- Fix leader-election timing bug — owner: Ben Carter — target: 2026-11-20 — status: in review.
- Post-deploy continuity script + verification harness — owner: Evelyn Hart — target: 2026-11-22 — status: in progress.
- Latency anomaly detector and tenant token guardrails — owner: Platform Observability — target: 2026-11-30 — status: planned.

Verification session: Tue 2026-11-17 10:00–11:00 PST (confirmed) — we will run a cloned workload and share traces. Please confirm attendees and any specific test scenarios you want covered.

Attachments: Incident_Chronicle_AcmeCloud_20261117.pdf (final), Mitigation-Checklist-AcmeCloud.xlsx (live)

Thanks for working with us on this; we appreciate the partnership and want to make validation as frictionless as possible.

Best,
Naomi

From: Michael Torres <michael.torres@acmecloud.com>

Cc: support@acmecloud.com, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Updated chronicle and confirmation of verification session - AcmeCloud

Thanks Naomi — received and appreciated. The timeline and actions look clear. Our SREs (cc’d) will join the 11/17 session; I also asked them to prepare the top two production queries that most closely match our streaming profile so we can validate continuity.

Please include the replay instructions in the Drive doc so we can run a secondary verification from our side later in the week. If the canary finishes cleanly on 11/20 and verification passes, we’ll mark the incident closed on our side.

—Michael
Michael Torres
Head of Platform Engineering
AcmeCloud
